Auckland University Walk Observation!

This is an exploration of people’s movement and actvities during walks around the University of Auckland. It looks at patterns in crowd size, activities, weather conditions, and time of day aross different University of Auckland campuses.

Runners/joggers Across Different Weather Conditions

This plot shows how different weather conditions can affect the number of runners/joggers.

Box plot showing the distribution of runners/joggers across different weather conditions including cloudy, rainy, sunny, and windy weather. Cloudy weather conditions show the highest number of runners/joggers on average, followed by sunny, windy, and rainy weather.

Average Running Activity Across UOA Campuses

This plot compares the average number of runners/joggers observed at City campus and Grafton campus.

Bar chart comparing average number of runners/joggers between City Campus and Grafton Campus, with Grafton Campus showing a higher average number of runners/joggers.

Activities Observed by Time of Day and Campus

This plot looks at how observed activities vary across different times of the day and between campuses.

Stacked proportional bar chart showing observed activities of walking, running/jogging, and cycling across hours of the day between City Campus and Grafton Campus. Walking is the most commonly observed activity across most times of the day.

Conclusion

Overall, weather conditions, campus location, and time of day all have an effect on the patterns of people’s movement and activity around the University of Auckland.
